subject.title: [Feature]: Self-hosted STT/TTS provider support in webchat (Route webchat TTS through the gateway instead of browser Speech API)

question: Should WebChat add core Gateway-backed Read aloud and editable batch dictation now, using `messages.tts` for TTS and `tools.media.audio` for STT, and what explicit fallback/privacy behavior should those controls have?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but accepting browser microphone audio and provider-backed playback/transcription in the core WebChat surface crosses product, privacy, auth-provider, and security-boundary decisions that code review cannot settle alone.

options.title: Split and land provider-backed core slices
options.body: Require a refreshed TTS PR using scoped media tickets and a separate editable STT PR reusing `tools.media.audio`, each with redacted real WebChat proof and explicit fallback behavior.

options.title: Limit WebChat voice to Talk for now
options.body: Keep current realtime Talk as the only built-in microphone path and leave one-off dictation/read-aloud requests open until a broader voice UX direction is decided.

options.title: Defer to plugin or external UI work
options.body: Decline core WebChat voice controls for now and ask self-hosted voice users to use media uploads, Talk relay, or external/plugin UI surfaces until core exposes a narrower extension point.

recommendation.title: Split and land provider-backed core slices
recommendation.body: Require a refreshed TTS PR using scoped media tickets and a separate editable STT PR reusing `tools.media.audio`, each with redacted real WebChat proof and explicit fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the prior WebChat dictation implementation and the active read-aloud candidate, and this decision centers on the same UI/Gateway voice boundary.
